title: Linklaters announces firmwide roll-out of Legora's generative AI platform
author: Legora

dom.t: Legora partnerships: Adoption needs selected workflows and training

st.t: Legora partnerships: Adoption needs selected workflows and training
st.an: The source supports the platform-led expansion narrative by documenting Linklaters’ firmwide deployment across 30 offices and positioning Legora alongside existing proprietary tools. Its claimed workflow and client benefits are presented as intended outcomes and executive testimony rather than measured productivity, accuracy or client results. It does not materially address the cluster’s emphasis on training or selected use cases.
qs: Embedding Legora across all 30 offices is the latest step in Linklaters’ strategy to support the world’s leading corporates, banks, funds and financial sponsors on their most complex, cross-border mandates.

It builds on Linklaters’ suite of Gen AI and technology tools, including proprietary chatbot Laila, online due diligence platform ReportIQ, and CreateiQ 2.0, the firm’s contract lifecycle management platform.

kp.k: Linklaters announces generative AI deployment across all 30 offices
kp.d: The September 22, 2025 Legora newsroom announcement reports Linklaters’ firmwide implementation of its legal generative AI platform. It presents deployment across all 30 offices as part of the firm’s strategy for supporting corporates, banks, funds and financial sponsors on complex cross-border mandates.
qs: Linklaters has announced the firmwide implementation of Legora's market-leading Generative AI platform tailored for legal professionals.

Embedding Legora across all 30 offices is the latest step in Linklaters’ strategy to support the world’s leading corporates, banks, funds and financial sponsors on their most complex, cross-border mandates.

kp.k: Platform targets research, drafting, review and workflow acceleration
kp.d: Legora describes the platform as designed to simplify workflows and accelerate research, drafting and reviewing at scale while enhancing lawyers’ strategic advice. These are stated purposes rather than quantified findings about productivity or service quality.
qs: Legora is designed to simplify workflows, accelerate research, drafting and reviewing at scale, and enhance the market-leading strategic advice that Linklaters provides.

kp.k: Legora supplements Linklaters’ existing legal technology suite
kp.d: The announcement positions Legora alongside, rather than as a replacement for, Linklaters’ existing tools: proprietary chatbot Laila, online due diligence platform ReportIQ and contract lifecycle management platform CreateiQ 2.0. In a customer quotation carried by Legora, Firmwide Managing Partner Paul Lewis reports that teams are already using Legora alongside the firm’s generative AI suite and characterises the partnership as strengthening client support.
qs: It builds on Linklaters’ suite of Gen AI and technology tools, including proprietary chatbot Laila, online due diligence platform ReportIQ, and CreateiQ 2.0, the firm’s contract lifecycle management platform.

More than equipping our teams with the best tools in an AI-enabled world, our partnership with Legora further strengthens our capabilities and enhances the support we are able to provide our global clients.
We are already using it alongside our suite of Gen AI tools and we are energised by how our teams are harnessing it to deliver for our clients on their most complex, cross-border mandates.

cl.s: Concrete claim or prediction about how AI changes legal services, the legal profession, or legal markets (or, for a cross-domain source, its own domain)

pts.k: Legora’s newsroom presents its platform as accelerating legal workflows and augmenting strategic advice; Linklaters’ managing partner says the partnership already strengthens capabilities and client support.
pts.d: The article, authored by team Legora, describes simplification of workflows and faster research, drafting and review at scale as intended platform benefits, rather than quantified outcomes. Paul Lewis, Linklaters’ Firmwide Managing Partner, separately asserts that the partnership strengthens the firm's capabilities and that teams are already using Legora alongside other generative AI tools on complex cross-border mandates. The framing is augmentation of lawyers through an expanded tool suite, not autonomous replacement. No claim is made about staffing reductions, fees or displacement of other providers.

cl.s: Evidence basis offered for the claim (data, benchmarks, cases, experience, authority, or none)

pts.k: The source offers a rollout announcement and executive testimony about current use, but no measured evidence of performance improvements.
pts.d: The announced firmwide implementation provides evidence of adoption, while Lewis supplies a qualitative account of teams' use and perceived benefits. The article does not provide time savings, quality measurements, benchmarks, detailed client cases or comparisons with prior workflows. Legora CEO Max Junestrand expresses commitment to continued collaboration and support rather than reporting independently measured outcomes.

cl.s: Stated or implied timeframe, conditions or qualifications under which the claim holds

pts.k: The September 22, 2025 announcement describes existing use and a firmwide rollout across 30 offices, with continued collaboration but no dated performance targets.
pts.d: Lewis's statement places use of Legora in the present at publication. The article describes embedding the platform across all 30 offices without specifying an implementation completion date. Benefits are situated within Linklaters’ existing technology strategy: Legora supplements Laila, ReportIQ and CreateiQ 2.0 rather than replacing the tool suite. The wording 'designed to' qualifies the workflow benefits as intended capabilities; no deadline or magnitude for their achievement is given.

cl.s: Who is affected and how (market segment, role, firm type, clients, or the public)

pts.k: The claimed benefits concern Linklaters’ legal teams globally and their large corporate and financial-sector clients.
pts.d: Lawyers and teams across Linklaters’ 30 offices are the intended users, with research, drafting and review identified as affected activities. The claimed downstream benefit is enhanced strategic advice and support for corporates, banks, funds and financial sponsors handling complex cross-border matters. The source does not extend these claims to individual consumers, unmet civil legal need or the legal labour market generally.
